A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Hallo3 and provide readable text, equations, seven tables and twelve figures. Both contain 12 pages ending with references; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original benchmark comparisons, generated examples, conditioning ablations, motion-frame experiments and CFG-scale results.

after.justification: Section 4 retains these original quantitative experiments and qualitative generation results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same CogVideoX backbone, audio cross-attention, identity reference network, face conditioning, two-stage training and motion-frame extrapolation procedure.

E1.justification: Training still uses HDTF, YouTube and movie footage. Evaluation retains HDTF, Celeb-V, the same wild portrait scenarios and textual control of subjects, foregrounds and backgrounds.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 and the qualitative comparisons retain SadTalker, DreamTalk, AniPortrait and Hallo. Figures 11–12 retain CogVideoX as the textual-controllability comparator.

E3.justification: The reported settings remain unchanged, including two 20,000-step training phases, 49-frame generation, the 34-case wild evaluation and all evaluation metrics and ablation configurations.

E4.justification: Sections 4.3–4.4 retain the same audio and identity conditioning ablations, motion-frame sweep, CFG-scale analysis and textual-controllability examples. No additional analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, uncertainty bars or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All seven tables retain their numerical entries, and the qualitative figures retain the same examples and findings. For example, the proposed method's HDTF FID/FVD remain 20.359/160.838 and Celeb-V FID/FVD remain 43.271/355.272.

T1.justification: The mathematical mappings and conditioning constructions in Section 3 are unchanged. Neither version contains a separate theorem or proof development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same novelty claim and contributions concerning DiT-based portrait animation, identity preservation, audio conditioning, video extrapolation and dynamic scenes.

C2.justification: The explanations of conditioning mechanisms and lip-synchronization tradeoffs are unchanged. The limitations concerning intricate expressions, varying illumination and diverse interactions, along with safety considerations, are also retained.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the advertised visualization/source-code access point from a GitHub repository to the project website. Implementation and hardware disclosures are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish any change in actual resource availability.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning and all 51 reference entries are unchanged.

P1.justification: The author block adds Shanghai Academy of AI for Science as an affiliation for Siyu Zhu, and the front-matter link and version stamp change. The scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Several figures are compressed or re-encoded, and Figure 7 changes from separately embedded images and text to a single raster image. Figures 2 and 5 show visible grain and reduced color detail. Figure content, captions and table structures remain the same.

improvement.justification: The scientific content and numerical evidence are unchanged, but v3 visibly reduces photographic fidelity in Figures 2 and 5 and lowers the resolution of Figure 7. This modestly weakens inspection of visual detail in a paper about realistic portrait generation. The affiliation and access-link updates do not offset that limited presentation loss.
